title: Problem 3
statement_text: For integers $k \geq 4$ and $t \geq k - 1$, what is the maximum chromatic number of $K_k$-free graphs of tree-width at most $t$?
context_text: Every graph of tree-width $t$ is $t$-degenerate, hence $(t+1)$-colourable, and $K_{t+1}$ shows this is tight. The authors prove that triangle-free graphs of tree-width at most $t$ have chromatic number at most $\lceil(t+3)/2\rceil$, and that this is tight. More generally, define $g(t,2)=g(0,k)=1$ for all $t\ge0$, $k\ge2$, and $g(t,k)=\lceil(t+1)/2\rceil+g(\lfloor(t-1)/2\rfloor,k-1)$ for $t\ge1$, $k\ge3$; they prove that for all $t\ge0$ and $k\ge2$ there is a $K_k$-free graph of tree-width at most $t$ with chromatic number at least $g(t,k)$. Here $g(t,3)=\lceil(t+3)/2\rceil$ for $t\ge1$ (so the case $k=3$ is completely resolved) and $g(t,k)>(1-\frac{1}{2^{k-2}})t$. This lower bound motivates the question for $k\ge4$, which the authors were not able to resolve. In the list colouring setting the analogous question is easy: $K_{t,t^t}$ has tree-width $t$ but is not colourable from some assignment of lists of size $t$.

title: Problem 4
statement_text: For integers $g \geq 4$ and $t \geq g - 1$, what is the maximum chromatic number of graphs of tree-width at most $t$ and girth at least $g$?
context_text: The construction of Blanche Descartes produces $d$-degenerate graphs of girth six that are not $d$-colorable, and Kostochka and Nešetřil generalise this to graphs of arbitrarily large girth, showing no improvement is possible via degeneracy alone. The paper asks whether bounding tree-width instead of degeneracy yields a girth-dependent improvement analogous to Theorem 1.
